children: The 10-year Treasury yield has been higher for seven consecutive months through September, tying the longest such streak since 1970, according to Jefferies data shared by Carl Quintanilla.

The chart tracks consecutive months in which 10-year yields were higher, with data spanning September 1970 through September 2026. The current seven-month run matches the longest streak shown in the series.

The accompanying chart showed several shorter streaks over the decades, but only a handful reaching seven months. The previous seven-month streaks visible in the chart occurred around 1977-78 and 2010, with the current run matching those peaks.

The latest streak comes as Treasury yields have climbed sharply. The 10-year yield stood at 5.17% on Thursday, up 4 basis points, after jumping 16 basis points Wednesday to 5.12%, its highest level since July 2007.

The move has come amid elevated expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening, with markets pricing a greater than 70% chance of an October rate hike on Wednesday as investors responded to hawkish central-bank commentary and renewed inflation pressures.

title: 10-year yield ties longest monthly streak since 1970
